cells.note: The docs name another PingOne environment as a trusted issuer. The person does not resolve to a local user: p1.userId is ignored.
A PingOne token is a signed JWT with iss, aud, exp and iat, and the docs say p1-prefixed claims are dropped when a token comes from outside. Not run.
Platform oidc takes any OIDC issuer, and a PingOne token is plain OIDC. Not run.
No source shows a PingOne environment issuing an ID-JAG. Check before relying on it.
A real PingFederate token, with its JWKS URL as the key source, was accepted as the actor token. Taken during the flag period; not re-run since general availability.
Needs a JWT access token. Our default token manager issued opaque reference tokens, which Authorize cannot accept. Add a JWT token manager.

The pf-test identity exists. A PingFederate token with matching claims was refused on the MCP door and the LLM route and no accepted or rejected line appeared in the gateway log. Open question for Ping.
PingFederate 13.1.3 issued ID-JAGs. Authplane, once told to trust it, redeemed one. Two other servers refused it: no kid in the header, and a signature failure.
The 10 Nov 2026 release note names PingAM among the trusted issuers. We have not run one.
The docs' own example is PingAM on PingOne Advanced Identity Cloud: the realm issuer URL and its jwk_uri.
Platform oidc takes any OIDC issuer. Not run.
No source shows PingAM issuing an ID-JAG.
Third-party issuers are allowed. Do not tick Require Not-before: an Okta token has no nbf. The claim shape was tried only with a token we signed ourselves.
Any server that issues signed JWT access tokens with aud, exp, iat and iss fits. Not run with Okta.
Platform oidc takes any OIDC issuer. Pin the calling application with RequiredClaims on cid. Not run.
Okta Cross App Access issues ID-JAGs that live 300 seconds. Our resource server trusts it. PingFederate as the redeemer of an Okta ID-JAG is not shown.
Third-party issuers are allowed. The Issuer ends in a slash and an Auth0 token has no nbf. The claim shape was tried only with a token we signed ourselves.
Fits if the token is a signed JWT access token. Issuers must match exactly, trailing slash included. Not run.
Platform oidc takes any OIDC issuer. Pin azp with RequiredClaims. Not run.
No source shows Auth0 issuing an ID-JAG.
Third-party issuers are allowed. v1.0 and v2.0 have different issuer strings, so each needs its own trusted issuer. Both carry nbf. Tried only with a token we signed ourselves.
One external server can list several Issuers: add the v1.0 and the v2.0 string if you accept both. Not run.
Platform oidc takes any OIDC issuer, but one identity holds one Issuer, so v1.0 and v2.0 need two identities. Not run.
No source shows Microsoft Entra ID issuing an ID-JAG.
An RFC 9068 token carries every claim PingOne can require. Tried only with a token we signed ourselves.
The docs ask for a signed JWT access token that is broadly RFC 9068 compliant.
Platform oidc takes any OIDC issuer. Not run.
RFC 9068 describes an access token. An ID-JAG has its own header typ, oauth-id-jag+jwt, so an access-token issuer is not enough.

Any signed JWT with a JWKS URL fits the form, but this surface cannot pin a subject or a claim: only the issuer and the audiences. With Audiences blank, every service account in the cluster is trusted.
The docs describe API access tokens. Nothing says a cluster's service-account token fits. Not run.
A live identity, k8s-sensor, trusts the cluster's issuer with AllowAnySubject on. The deck lists a projected token read as a deployment model. Acceptance of a token was not re-run in that note.
A service-account token is not an ID-JAG: the typ must be oauth-id-jag+jwt and an IdP mints it after a token exchange.
Same limits as Kubernetes: issuer and audiences only. The cluster id in the issuer path is part of the exact match.
Not mentioned in the docs. Not run.
Two live identities, eks-sensor-a and eks-sensor-b, each trust their cluster's OIDC issuer and pin the pod's service account. Acceptance of a token was not re-run in that note.
A service-account token is not an ID-JAG.
This surface cannot pin repository, workflow or environment, so a job from any repository that can request your audience would be trusted. Prefer Federated Identity for CI.
Not mentioned in the docs. Not run.
Per-job CI/CD tokens are a deployment model on slide 40. The sub is composite, so pin repository, workflow and environment with RequiredClaims. Not run on our tenant.
A job token is not an ID-JAG.
Issuer and audiences only: no pin on project path or ref. Prefer Federated Identity for CI.
Not mentioned in the docs. Not run.
Per-job CI/CD tokens (slide 40). Pin project_path and ref with RequiredClaims. Not run on our tenant.
A job token is not an ID-JAG.
A JWT-SVID is a signed JWT, but the surface cannot pin the SPIFFE ID in sub. Not run.
Not mentioned in the docs. Not run.
SPIFFE/SPIRE for mixed estates (slide 40). Our notes verify the SPIFFE to PingFederate leg; SPIFFE straight to the gateway is untested.
A JWT-SVID is not an ID-JAG.
The sensor's self-signed token authenticates its reports to the Privilege gateway. No PingOne exchange is involved.
The token is for the Privilege gateway, not for an API behind Authorize.
The sensor signs its own token and the console pins the key id: reports failed Unauthenticated when the key file was lost and recovered when the new key set was pasted in.
A sensor token is not an ID-JAG.
We trusted an issuer whose key we generated ourselves, with the key set pasted in, and exchanged its token. Taken during the flag period.
Works only if the key set is public HTTPS with no custom certificate, or you paste it (16 KB at most).
Pin the public keys with JWKS instead of JwksURI. Not run.
Any IdP that mints ID-JAGs can be trusted through an IdP connection with its entity id and JWKS URL.
